fine_lines.title: do vs make
fine_lines.explanation_ar: do للفعل نفسه: أعمال متكررة، واجبات، عدة أفعال معًا؛ ترى الفعل لكن لا تستطيع لمسه. make للنتيجة: صنع أو إنتاج شيء جديد يمكن غالبًا لمسه، وأيضًا للاختيار (make a decision) والكلام (make a speech, make a noise).
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Do" is the action itself: repeated jobs, obligations, several actions; you can see it but not touch it. "Make" is the result: creating or producing something you can usually touch; also for choosing (make a decision) and speaking (make a speech, make a noise).

examples.sentence: I do my homework every evening.
I made a cake for my mother.

fine_lines.title: make an exception vs make an example of
fine_lines.explanation_ar: make an exception = تسمح لشخص بشيء غير مسموح للآخرين (أمر جيد له). make an example of someone = تعاقب شخصًا أمام الجميع ليتعلم الآخرون (أمر سيئ له).
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Make an exception" = allow someone to do what others can't (good for them). "Make an example of someone" = punish someone publicly so others learn (bad for them).

examples.sentence: The class is full, but we'll make an exception for you.
The teacher made an example of the noisy student.

grammar.title: When to use do
grammar.explanation_ar: استعمل do: 1) للأعمال المتكررة (I do the dishes every night). 2) للواجبات (do homework). 3) كاختصار لعدة أفعال (do the laundry = wash, dry, fold). 4) بدل فعل واحد (do my hair = fix/wash، do a report = write).
grammar.explanation_en: Use "do": 1) for repeated jobs (I do the dishes every night); 2) for obligations (do homework); 3) as shorthand for several actions (do the laundry = wash, dry, fold); 4) to replace one verb (do my hair = fix/wash; do a report = write).
examples: I do the dishes every night.
Can you do a report on that?

grammar.title: When to use make
grammar.explanation_ar: استعمل make: 1) للخلق والصنع (make a cake). 2) للاختيار (make a decision). 3) للإنتاج المستمر (They make cars). 4) للكلام والأصوات (make a speech, make a noise).
grammar.explanation_en: Use "make": 1) to create (make a cake); 2) to choose (make a decision); 3) to produce (They make cars); 4) for speaking and sounds (make a speech, make a noise).

grammar.title: See it = do, touch it = make
grammar.explanation_ar: حيلة: مع do ترى الفعل بعينك لكن لا تمسكه. مع make توجد نتيجة يمكن غالبًا لمسها. do هو العمل، و make هو النتيجة: I do everything I can to make you happy.
grammar.explanation_en: Trick: with "do" you can see the action but not hold it. With "make" there is a result you can usually touch. Do = the action; make = the result: "I do everything I can to make you happy."
examples: I do everything I can to make you happy.
I did some work to make some money.

grammar.title: Exception: make the bed
grammar.explanation_ar: ترتيب السرير عمل متكرر، لكننا نقول make the bed وليس do the bed. ربما لأننا ننتج سريرًا مرتبًا جميلًا.
grammar.explanation_en: Making the bed is a repeated job, but we say "make the bed", not "do the bed". Maybe because we produce a tidy, nice bed.
examples: I make my bed every morning.
